correctness.rationale: For downsets, pseudocomplement is the set of points whose principal downset misses the operand. A second De Morgan counterexample yields two distinct minimal points with a common upper bound. The explicit injection \(a\mapsto(a,\neg a)\) proves \(b(H)\ge u(H)\). If \(b(H)=u(H)>0\), a third minimum or a nonminimal point supported on only one of the witness minima creates two distinct failing partners for a unary-bad first coordinate, forcing \(P=A_2\oplus Q\). Conversely that ordinal sum has exactly two failing singleton cross-pairs and two unary failures. The sharp bound follows from \(b(H)\ge2\), the equality classification, and a chain \(Q\) of \(h-4\) points. The higher-minimum formula counts disjoint ordered nonempty subsets. Exact implementation comparisons on 5,231 naturally labeled posets through six points and 200 ordinal-sum cases corroborate, without replacing, these all-size arguments.

value.rationale: The logical validity/invalidity distinction for Stone algebras is known; quantifying how many assignments fail is a motivated degree-of-satisfiability refinement. The main contribution is a complete, natural equality-case classification across all finite Heyting algebras, not merely a small improvement in a numerical bound. It determines the sharp satisfaction probability for every possible finite non-Stone carrier size and identifies exactly when unary and binary defect statistics coincide despite their universally equivalent identities. The arbitrary upper-poset family and the two same-unary/different-binary examples show that the result is not a restatement of the classical Stone criterion.
